full_judgment:
Md Muzammel Hossain J : This Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to remove the unauthorised pole of electric overhead line from the petitioner's land situated at Police Station Savar, Dhaka Collectorate, Touji No. 1131, Union/Touji 112, JL No. 566 (former), 81 (present) Mouza and Parganah- Palashbari Kashimpur SA Khatian No. 19(Former), 16(Present) Dag No. 363 (Former), 646 (Present) Jote No. 293 (Former), 1532 (Present) total 71 decimals of land and why their acts should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The petitioner being a citizen of Bangladesh is a renowned businessman both in Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia. The respondent No.1 is the General Manager, Dhaka Rural Electrification Samity and the respondent No. 2 is the Chairman, Rural Electrification Board. The petitioner having purchased the schedule land on 18-3-1974 from the recorded owner mutated his name and has been paying Government land development tax and possessing the same since purchase. The petitioner is a businessman having business both in Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia and taking advantage of his temporary absence from this country the respondents set up a pole almost in the middle of the petitioner's plot situated at Police Station Savar, Dhaka Collectorate, Touji No. 1131, Union/Touji 12, JL No. 566 (former), 81 (present), Mouza and Parganah Palashbari Kashimpur, SA Khatian No. 19 (former), 16 (Present) Dag No. 363 (Fonner), 646 (Present) Jote No. 293 (Former), 1532 (Present) measuring an area of 71 decimals of land. The petitioner on several occasions orally requested the respondents to remove the unauthorised pole and the respondents in this way or that way delayed the matter though they assured the petitioner on different occasions to remove the pole immediately. The petitioner was compelled to serve legal notices upon the respondents on 15-1-2002 and 7-2-2002 requesting them to remove the unauthorised electric pole failing which appropriate action would be taken. Thereafter, on 13-2-2002 the respondent No. 1 gave a reply to the legal notices dated 15-1-2002 and 7-2-2002 shifting the burden illegally upon the petitioner by asking him to pay all the expenses for such removal and to obtain necessary permission from the Authority of Savar Cantonment. Under the circumstances the petitioner again was compelled to serve another legal notice on 10-4-2002 upon the respondent No.1 stating specifically that unless the electrical pole is removed from the petitioner's plot the petitioner is not in a position to construct the proposed multistoried building, plan of which has been approved by the appropriate Authority of Savar Cantonment. Earlier on 18-6-2000, the petitioner submitted a proposed plan for constructing a multistoried building and the said proposal was accepted and approved vide Memo শাক্যবো/ন অ/নৃই/৫৩ dated 11-3-2001 (Annexure-E) by the Cantonment Executive Officer, Savar Cantonment, Dhaka.
